quests.instruction: Meera learns a poem for assembly by reading it silently, but when she stands in front of the school she freezes. What step was missing in her preparation?
quests.hint: Decide what is different between reading silently and performing.
quests.explanation: Saying the words aloud prepares her voice and memory for the real thing. Reading silently does not practise speaking.
quests.funFact: Saying words aloud can help them stick in memory, because speaking and hearing both play a part.

quests.instruction: Aarav's family drives up to a hill station. They pack water and hats, but the top is chilly and he shivers. What step was missing when packing?
quests.hint: Decide how the air changes as you go higher.
quests.explanation: Hills are cooler than the plains, so a warm layer is needed even when it is hot at home. A swimming costume or sunglasses do not help.
quests.funFact: Air gets cooler as you climb, falling by roughly six degrees for every thousand metres.

quests.instruction: Aanya hosts a birthday party and serves a nut cake. A guest who is allergic to nuts cannot eat anything. What step was missing?
options: Bake a Much Bigger Cake Instead 🎂
Invite Far Fewer Guests Next Time 🙈
quests.hint: Think about what she could have found out in advance.
quests.explanation: Asking before the party lets her choose food that everyone can eat. A bigger cake or fewer guests would not fix the problem.
quests.funFact: Invitations often include 'RSVP', from a French phrase meaning 'please reply'.

quests.instruction: Dev puts on his helmet and rides downhill, but his brakes are weak and he nearly crashes. What step was missing before he rode?
quests.hint: The clue is what a rider needs in order to stop safely.
quests.explanation: Brakes are what stop the bicycle, so checking them before a ride matters as much as wearing a helmet.
quests.funFact: The word 'bicycle' means 'two wheels', from Latin and Greek roots.

quests.instruction: Mina's hands are wet from washing up, and she reaches to switch on the fan. What step was missing?
quests.hint: Decide what water does around electricity.
quests.explanation: Water can carry electricity, so hands must be dry before touching switches or plugs.
quests.funFact: Ordinary tap water conducts electricity because of the minerals dissolved in it.

quests.instruction: Zoya sees a friendly-looking dog at the park and reaches out to pat it. It barks and she jumps back. What step was missing?
quests.hint: Work out who knows the dog best.
quests.explanation: The owner knows whether the dog is comfortable with strangers, so asking first keeps everyone safe. Patting from behind can startle a dog.
quests.funFact: Dogs communicate with their bodies, and a stiff posture can mean they are unsure.

quests.instruction: After blowing his nose, Aman puts the tissue in his pocket and goes to lunch. What steps were missing?
quests.correctAnswer: Bin the Tissue and Wash Up 🗑️
options: Bin the Tissue and Wash Up 🗑️
Wipe His Nose on His Sleeve 👕
Share the Tissue with a Friend 🤝
quests.hint: Remember where used tissues and dirty hands belong.
quests.explanation: A used tissue carries germs, so it goes in the bin and hands are washed before eating.
quests.funFact: Germs can survive on a used tissue for a while, so it is best not to carry it around.

quests.instruction: Karan's fingernails are long and have dirt under them. What routine would help?
options: Paint Them a Bright Shiny Colour 💅
quests.hint: Ask yourself how often nails grow.
quests.explanation: Nails keep growing and trap dirt, so trimming and cleaning them regularly keeps hands cleaner.
quests.funFact: Fingernails grow about three millimetres each month.

quests.instruction: Rohan shares his water bottle with a friend who has a cold, and feels ill the next day. What step was missing?
quests.correctAnswer: Keep His Own Bottle to Himself 🧴
options: Wash the Cap Only Once a Month 🫧
Keep His Own Bottle to Himself 🧴
quests.hint: Think about how germs travel from mouth to mouth.
quests.explanation: Bottles carry saliva, so sharing them can pass on germs. Each child keeping their own bottle avoids that.
quests.funFact: Colds spread most easily through tiny droplets and by touching shared objects.

quests.instruction: It is monsoon season and Ira's school bag gets soaked on the way, so her books are wet. What step was missing?
quests.correctAnswer: Put a Rain Cover on the Bag ☔
options: Carry the Bag Under One Arm 💪
Put a Rain Cover on the Bag ☔
quests.hint: Remember how to keep rain off the bag itself.
quests.explanation: A rain cover or waterproof bag keeps the books dry, even in heavy rain. Carrying the bag differently would not stop it getting wet.
quests.funFact: Waterproof fabrics are often coated so that water forms beads and rolls off.

quests.instruction: The lane is flooded after heavy rain, and Dev wants to wade across to a friend's house. What step was missing?
options: Take a Quick Shortcut Through It 🏃
quests.hint: Remember what could be hidden under the water.
quests.explanation: Floodwater can hide holes and sharp objects and carry germs, so a grown-up decides whether it is safe. Rolling up trousers does not make it safe.
quests.funFact: Moving floodwater can be stronger than it looks, even when it is shallow.

quests.instruction: Tara hurries along a wet pavement and slips on a smooth tile. What step was missing?
quests.correctAnswer: Slow Down and Watch Her Step 🐢
options: Slow Down and Watch Her Step 🐢
Close Her Eyes and Hurry On 🙈
quests.hint: Ask yourself how to keep your feet under you on a slippery surface.
quests.explanation: Wet tiles are slippery, so shorter, slower steps and watching the ground help prevent a fall. Hurrying makes slipping more likely.
quests.funFact: Smooth stone or tile can be much more slippery when wet than when dry.

quests.instruction: After the class party, the floor is covered in cups and streamers, and the teacher spends an hour tidying alone. What step was missing?
quests.hint: Remember how a big job gets smaller.
quests.explanation: When everyone helps, a big job becomes quick and nobody is left to do it alone.
quests.funFact: After matches at some tournaments, Japanese supporters have been seen tidying the stands before leaving.

quests.instruction: After a play in the school hall, the children leave the chairs scattered, and the next class cannot start. What step was missing?
quests.correctAnswer: Put the Chairs Back in Place 🪑
options: Put the Chairs Back in Place 🪑
quests.hint: Decide what the next group needs.
quests.explanation: Putting things back as they were means the hall is ready for the next class, and nobody has to fix someone else's mess.
quests.funFact: School halls are used for assemblies, lunches and sport, so furniture often has to be moved and moved back.

quests.instruction: Joy finishes using the school computer but leaves her account open on the screen. What step was missing?
options: Leave It On for the Next Child 🖥️
quests.hint: Remember who could use the screen after her.
quests.explanation: Logging out keeps her account private, and switching off saves power. Leaving it open lets anyone see or change her work.
quests.funFact: Logging out is a basic way to keep an online account private on a shared computer.

quests.instruction: Neha's sleeve nearly touches the flame as she stands next to a grown-up who is cooking. What step was missing before she stood by the stove?
quests.hint: Consider what could catch fire.
quests.explanation: Loose sleeves can drift into a flame and catch fire, so they are rolled up or tied back before working near heat.
quests.funFact: Cooks often wear fitted sleeves, because loose clothing is a fire risk near flames.

quests.instruction: Mina carries plates to the table but trips over a bag left in the doorway. What step was missing?
quests.hint: The clue is what is lying on the floor.
quests.explanation: A clear path means there is nothing to trip over when hands are full.
quests.funFact: Tripping over objects left on floors is one of the most common causes of falls at home.

quests.instruction: Raj leaves leftover curry on the counter overnight, and it smells off in the morning. What step was missing?
options: Stir It Again in the Morning 🥄
Cover It with a Warm Cloth 🧣
quests.hint: The key is keeping food cool.
quests.explanation: Cool temperatures slow the growth of germs in food, so leftovers go into the fridge soon after a meal.
quests.funFact: Germs in food grow fastest at warm temperatures, so food should not sit out for long in hot weather.

quests.instruction: Mina's friend tells her about a new game, and she downloads it on the family tablet without asking. What step was missing?
options: Tell Friends to Download It Too 👥
quests.hint: Consider who is responsible for the family tablet.
quests.explanation: A grown-up can check that the game is safe and suitable. Some apps cost money or are not meant for children.
quests.funFact: Apps carry age ratings that tell parents who they are designed for.

quests.instruction: Priya plays an online game and tells another player her password because they asked. What step was missing?
options: Give It to a Friend Who Asks 🤝
Use Her Name as the Password 📛
quests.hint: Work out who should know your password.
quests.explanation: A password protects an account, so it is kept private and shared only with a trusted grown-up.
quests.funFact: Strong passwords mix letters, numbers and symbols and avoid names or birthdays.

quests.instruction: Zoya reads an unkind message about her in a group chat and sends an angry reply at once. What step was missing?
quests.hint: Focus on getting help before reacting.
quests.explanation: A grown-up can help her decide what to do, and a pause stops the situation getting worse.
quests.funFact: Most apps let users block or report unkind messages.

quests.instruction: Anu feels sick on long car journeys when she reads a book in the back seat. What step would help most?
options: Eat a Big Greasy Meal First 🍟
quests.hint: The clue is what the eyes and the body feel when the car moves.
quests.explanation: Looking at the road and getting fresh air can help the eyes and body agree about the movement, so sickness is less likely. Reading in a moving car makes it worse.
quests.funFact: Travel sickness happens when the eyes and inner ears send mixed messages about movement.

quests.instruction: Dia's eyes itch after playing in a dusty field. What should she do?
options: Wipe Them with a Dirty Cloth 🧻
quests.hint: Consider washing out something very small.
quests.explanation: Clean water rinses dust away gently, while rubbing or a dirty cloth can scratch the eye or add germs.
quests.funFact: Blinking and tears help wash dust out of the eyes.

quests.instruction: Rita sleeps until noon every weekend and cannot fall asleep on Sunday night. What habit was missing?
quests.correctAnswer: Wake at a Similar Time Each Day ⏰
options: Wake at a Similar Time Each Day ⏰
Sleep Even Later on Sunday Morning 🛌
quests.hint: Work out what keeps the body's clock steady.
quests.explanation: Waking at about the same time each day helps the body clock stay steady, so sleep comes more easily at night.
quests.funFact: Staying close to the same wake-up time, even at weekends, helps the body's sleep rhythm.

quests.instruction: Aman promised to return a friend's book on Monday, but on Friday it is still at the bottom of his bag. What step was missing?
quests.hint: Think about how to remember something that is not part of the daily routine.
quests.explanation: A reminder note or alarm helps him remember a promise that is not part of the usual routine.
quests.funFact: A sticky note on the door is a classic reminder that is hard to miss.

quests.instruction: Ravi told his sister he would help with her puzzle after dinner. After dinner he starts a game and forgets. What step was missing?
quests.hint: Think about what comes before starting something new.
quests.explanation: Keeping a promise comes before starting something new, so he should help first and play afterwards.
quests.funFact: Keeping promises helps others trust you, which is a big part of friendship.

quests.instruction: Priya knows on Tuesday that she cannot go to her friend's party on Saturday, but she only tells her on the day. What step was missing?
quests.hint: The clue is what the friend needs in order to plan.
quests.explanation: Telling her friend early gives time to change plans. Saying nothing leaves the friend waiting and worried.
quests.funFact: Hosts often need to know how many guests are coming so they can plan food and space.

quests.instruction: After finishing any routine, which quick check helps catch a missing step?
quests.correctAnswer: Run Through the Steps Once More 📋
options: Skip the Very Last Step Today 🙈
Run Through the Steps Once More 📋
quests.hint: Work out how to look back over what you have done.
quests.explanation: Going through the steps one more time helps spot anything that was left out. Skipping steps or starting something else does not.
quests.funFact: Proofreaders read through a text one more time to catch what was missed.

quests.instruction: Dev borrows a ball from the school cupboard, plays with it and puts it back, but the ball is flat and muddy. What step was missing?
quests.correctAnswer: Check It Is Clean and Undamaged 🔍
options: Check It Is Clean and Undamaged 🔍
Swap It for a Different Ball 🔄
Keep It for Another Week or Two 📅
quests.hint: Think about the condition in which he leaves things for the next user.
quests.explanation: Checking and cleaning an item before returning it leaves it ready for the next person.
quests.funFact: A ball can lose its shape if it is left in a hot place, so it is best stored in a cool, dry cupboard.

quests.instruction: Aanya's class visits a museum. She stops to look at an exhibit and finds herself separated from the group. What step was missing?
quests.hint: Consider how two people can keep an eye on each other.
quests.explanation: A buddy notices if you fall behind, so neither of you is left alone. Wandering or waiting alone makes getting lost more likely.
quests.funFact: The buddy system is used by school groups, swimmers and divers to keep everyone safe.
